sourceDesc.p: Born digital: no previous source exists.

div.note: The Administrator sits in a massive room of screens, giving orders to RED and BLU team over a large intercom.

cbml:panel.cbml:caption: One week ago...
cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: CLICK
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator clicks a lighter on, and lights a cigarette.
The Administrator smokes the cigarette she lit.
Close up view of The Administrator's eye.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Alert, Blue Team! Our Control Point is being contested!
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator plugs something into an audio jack.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Well done, Red Team. You have captured the Control Point.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator plugs something into another audio jack.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Capture our Control Point, Blue Team!
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator plugs into the BLU audio jack again.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Red Team! Defend our Control Point!
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator plugs into the RED audio jack again.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Hm. Well now. What's that Spy up to?
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator sits in front of a center console, plugging into different audio jacks to give out commands. The room is full of screens featuring actual Team Fortress 2 gameplay.

div.note: The Administrator gives a command to BLU Team (mirroring Meet The Spy), but gets interrupted by Ms. Pauling

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: ALERT!
A Red Spy is in the base!
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator clutches a microphone as her cigarette falls from her lips

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: UNPLUG
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator unplugs the microphone from the central console.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Ugh.
The SCOUT, you idiots.
He's disguised as the Scout.
A Red Spy is in the base?
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator watches BLU attempt to find the RED Spy. Soldier can be heard through the screen.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Is there a problem, Miss Pauling?
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator sits, smoking her cigarette.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: What... Makes you say-
Because you're hovering. And you only hover when there's a problem.
Let's have it.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling speeks to The Administrator, clutching a piece of paper.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: We did a background check on the mercenaries.
Standard protocol, nothing-
Sometime today, please.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling speeks to The Administrator, clutching a piece of paper. The Administrator rolls her eyes.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It's the... BLU Soldier and RED Demoman.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling speeks to The Administrator, looking at a piece of paper. The Administrator seems intrigued.

div.note: Miss Pauling shows The Administrator a bunch of pictures of the BLU Soldier and RED Demoman being friends together.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It looks like they've become...
...friends, Administrator.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling looks quite distraught.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: TWITCH
For how long?

cbml:balloon.emph: How did we not know about this?

cbml:panel.note: The Administrator's eye twitches as she hears about the news.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Within the last six months, Administrator.
As far as we can tell, they met at a projectile weapons expo.
It, uh... Seems to have blossomed into a lifelong friendship.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator inspects the images of BLU Soldier and RED Demoman. In order, the pictures feature: Soldier and Demoman visiting Las Vegas, Soldier and Demoman visiting a large gravel pit, Soldier and Demoman at a basketball game, Soldier and Demoman visiting an eye museum, and Soldier and Demoman out on a boat, fishing.

div.note: The Administrator and Miss Pauling discuss what to do.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Heh. You know, forgetting for a minute that we don't condone friendship, it's sort of...
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling smiles. The Administrator seethes in rage.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Almost...
Uh...
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling frowns. The Administrator glances at her.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Reprehensible. Totally and completely reprehensible.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator thinks for a moment.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: We are in agreement, Miss Pauling.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator speaks, cigarette in hand.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: This friendship is a profound betrayal of our trust.
Why, friends could easily...
Could...
cbml:panel.note: A close up of The Administrator's face.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Miss Pauling, you strike me as the sort of person who would have friends.
Tell me...
What do they do?
Um. Go skating...
Look at gun catalogs...
Sometimes we just talk...
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator looks at her screens as her and Miss Pauling speak.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Talking? Friendship is even worse than I thought.
No, this won't do at all.
If they talk, Miss Pauling, they might talk about work.
And if they talk about work...
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator blows a puff of smoke as she monologues.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: They might talk about us.
cbml:panel.note: Close up of The Administrator's face.

div.note: In a smoke filled room, The Administrator and Miss Pauling finish their chat.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: This is what we will do.
Call Mister Hale.
Tell him that we have some custom orders for him.
Tell him money is no object.
And tell him we need them right now.
Yes, ma'am. Anything else?
Open channels to our two new best friends.
I have a proposition for each of them.
In my experience, Miss Pauling, nothing kills a friendship faster...
cbml:panel.note: Sitting in front of her console, The Administrator lays our her plan to Miss Pauling.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: ...than a healthy competition.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator looks at pictures of the BLU Soldier and RED Demoman pulled up on monitors. They are screenshots from the game, and not drawn by hand.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Sir, you shouldn't jump yet! We're too low!It's not safe!
cbml:panel.note: A plane flies above with a blue sky in the background.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: I know the risks Jerry! But I've got damn good men down there who need me!
Tell them It's not safe enough!
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale prepares to jump out of the plane; holding a bag over his shoulder while Jerry sits in the foreground, flying the plane.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: But Sir, I can climb to a safe altitude.
It will literally take seconds, if you'll just-
cbml:panel.note: Jerry sits in the cockpit, facing away as he flys the plane.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Tell those men down there you can "climb to a safe altitude"!
Me, I'd rather get down there and tell them myself...
with my bare hands!
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale speaks in front of a red background, with an aggressive look on his face.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: At least take the backup parachute!
cbml:panel.note: Hale jumps out of the plane, with the same blue sky in the background.

cbml:panel.cbml:caption: Reader, if you thought the first two pages of my comic contained too much bare-knuckle excitement, then get ready to have your eyes break from widening in surprise and your comic-holding hands fall off your very arms when you get a look at the rest of this action-packed ish, starring me...
cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: SAXTON HAAAALE!
cbml:panel.cbml:caption: If this sensational issue doesn't stop your adrenaline-gorged heart for five entire seconds, I will send you a notarized cerificate confirming you do not exist!

How am I so sure? I have self-confidence! Also, just three pages from now, I will beat up a parking lot full of hippies. I certainly wouldn't blame you if you skip ahead! I am! For the rest of you, read on as I...
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale flies down through the air, with the plane flying away in the background.

div.cbml:caption: ...barrel roll directing into my office at Mann Co. Headquarters!

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Mr. Bidwell! How did my landing compare to yesterday's?
Be frank with me now. I'm made of stern stuff.
Hup hup!
Hahrup!
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale crashes through the wall of Mann Co. Headquarters, while performing a barrel roll. A distant shot of him dropping in from the plane with a parachute is displayed underneath the rest of the panels.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Tears were brought to the eyes, Sir.
Your breakfast steak.
cbml:panel.note: Mr. Bidwell and Mr. Reddy greet Saxton Hale in the kitchen, holdng a plate of steak and a clipboard.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It's the most important steak of the day, Bidwell.
Mr. Reddy! How's accounts?
You're now the sixth richest man in America, Mr. Hale.

div.note: Saxton Hale rips a chunk of steak off and eats it, as Mr. Reddy reads to him off of a clipboard.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Top drawer! Send the other five a congratualtory bouquet and my "You're a dead man" form letter. / What's next?
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale stands in front of a bear statue, pointing up to the sky as Mr. Reddy stands behind him.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: There's a group of hippies protesting the parking lot again... / Guns, Sir. They're against them.
The scoundrels! What have they got their smelly ponytails in a twist about this time? / Fine. I'll beat tem to death with my bare hands!
cbml:panel.note: The two men walk through through a large building, towards the mentioned parking lot.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: TF Industries is holding on line one, Sir.
What? Why didn't you say so, man! Don't leave Helen on hold!
cbml:panel.note: Mr. Reddy stands behind Saxton, holding a large brick phone in hand. Saxton looks back with frustration.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Helennnn! You chain-smoking seductress! / Do you still like steak dinners and sex with handsome men?
Mister Hale, this is Miss Pauling. I work for Miss...

div.note: Saxton Hale speaks into the phone with a confident look on his face.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Excellent! My offer still stands! What can I do for you, Miss Pauling?
We need to resolve a, uh... / Personnel problem. / We were hoping you could provide the incentivies.
cbml:panel.note: Saxton walks pushes open a door and walks into a room full of darkness.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It just so happens my boys in R and D sent up a few crates of highly experimental new ordinance they wanted me to take for a text drive. / Why don't I send those over? Hold on, Bidwell's gesturing frantically to me about something...
cbml:panel.note: Saxton Hale speaks menacingly into the phone while looking away.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Sir, those were the weapons you asked us to send up so you could destroythem before the senate investigation.
I have no idea what you're-- Ooo, right. That poor monkey.
Well, nevermind that. Helping Helen out's more important.
cbml:panel.note: Mr. Bidwell stands with a finger pointed to his lip. Saxton holds the phone next to him.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Also getting someone else's fingerprints on these things as soon as possible. I won't lie to you Bidwell, we are in a lot of trouble here.
Miss Pauling, still there?
cbml:panel.note: Saxton speaks into the phone with a serious expression in a black background.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Um... I heard everything you said, Mister Hale.
Fannnntastic. And?
We'll take them.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling sits in her office, speaking on the phone to Saxton on the other end.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Problem solved! / Mr. Reddy! We're going to need some ambulances! Mr. Bidwell! I need an alibi that puts me anywhere but the parking lot for the next seven minutes! / Let's go kill some hippies!
cbml:panel.note: Saxton speaks out of frame as he throws the phone to Mr. Reddy. Mr. Reddy stands in frame ready to catch the phone.

div.note: Demoman and his mother discuss his laziness at only holding three jobs.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: For the last time, Mum. I don't have to go to work. It's me morning off.
"Morning off"? Oh, lord help me, you've been fired. I knew it.
cbml:panel.note: An overview shot of the Degroot's large, beautiful mansion.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: *Sigh* No, Mum. It's just the one mornin'.
Oh, well that's fine then, I'm sure.
I just wish your poor ol' Da could take a morning off. From SPINNIN' IN HIS GRAVE AT YOUR IDLENESS!
I'm holdin' down three jobs, Mum.
Three jobs! Ha! Listen to him!
Tavish, your father, god rest him, had twenty-six jobs! And he still found the time to teach you the family trade!
I made five million dollars last year, Mum. We live in a mansion.
cbml:panel.note: Demoman pours some tea for himself while bantering with his mother.

div.note: Demoman and his mother have a conversation about family history.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Aye, and who told you to buy a bloody mansion, I'd like to know.
These're your prime earning years. You're halfway to retirement already.
Mark me, boy: No Demoman worth his sulfur ever had an eye in his head past THIRTY!
Mm-hm. Tea's up, Mum.
cbml:panel.note: Demoman brings his mother the tea.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It wasn't easy bringing you Scottish, lad.
Lean years. In those days you could bomb mercs all day and still not have enough for a loaf of bread.
Yer Da walked fifteen miles in the rain to blow up the Queen of England for a nickel!
I'll get more jobs, Mum. I promise.
I just hate to see you squandering your gifts.
I know, Mum.
I miss him, Tavish. Every day.
cbml:panel.note: Demoman and his mother reminisce about Mr. Degroot.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: I know, Mum.
Bloody hell, me one mornin' off...
Drink your tea, Mum. I'll be right back.
cbml:panel.note: A knock at the door interrupts their reminiscing.

div.note: Miss Pauling meets with Demoman, and offers him something worth destroying a friendship.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Mister Degroot?
Tavish? Who is it?
Someone from work, Mum!
Ask him has he got any more jobs!
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling is at the door.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Here, I know you. You're that wee lass, who works with the angry lady who's always screamin' at us while we fight.
cbml:panel.note: Demoman points at Miss Pauling.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: She's not so bad once you get to know her.
Really, and what's she want, then?
cbml:panel.note: Demoman leans against the wall.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: She'd like you to kill your best friend.
In exchange, we'll give you this.
Are ye seriously asking me to betray me best mate for a weapon?
HA! I've got a little more integrity than that, Lass. I...
Oh my.
What's your name, you dirty girl?
cbml:panel.note: Demoman looks in awe at the box, face lit up by its contents.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: This... is the Eyelander.
SHING!
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling holds the Eyelander over her.
Demoman now holds the Eyelander triumphantly straight up.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Pattern-welded Damascus steel.
Harmonically balanced.
Slow-forged for generations in the bowels of captured English kings.
...headddds...
cbml:panel.note: Demoman clutches the Eyelander in awe.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: headheadheadheadheadheadheadhead
cbml:panel.note: Demoman runs with the Eyelander, eyeing up a nearby statue.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: WHOCK!
cbml:panel.note: Demoman chops off the head of the statue.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Um.
And it's haunted.
cbml:panel.note: Demoman smiled and clutches the sliced head. Miss Pauling watches.

div.note: Pauling tempts Demoman with further weaponry and some bad news about his friend.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Blast ye, woman. Making a man choose between his best friend and a sword.
Ach. No. No, I couldn't. Soldier's me best mate.
cbml:panel.note: A distraught Demoman.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Tell you what. Why don't I leave them here, and you can think about it.
"Them"?
cbml:panel.note: Demoman stares at Miss Pauling in disbelief.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: I should get going.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling walks away, revealing three giant boxes containing other weapons for Demoman.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Oh, and Mister Degroot?
Your friend's employers made him the same offer.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling glances behind, smirking.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: He said yes, Mister Degroot.
Enjoy your morning off.
cbml:panel.note: Miss Pauling waves and continues to walk away. Demoman clutches the Eyelander and stares.

div.note: In a black and white styled apartment, a hired hand attempts to visit one Mister Jane Doe.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: This is the place.
cbml:panel.note: The hired hand shuffles through a dark apartment building.

body.p: NO SOLICITORS! DO NOT TEST ME

cbml:panel.note: Notes on "Mister Jane Doe's" door.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Hht. For the money we paid you to find it, it had better be.
You're wasting my time. Go knock.
cbml:panel.note: The hired hand reaches Soldier's door. Bullet holes and two large circular flaps are visible.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: KNOCK KNOCK
Good.
Now duck.
cbml:panel.note: The hired hand knocks on the door.

div.note: Soldier tries and fails to kill the hired hand.

cbml:panel.note: Two shotgun blasts shoot through the door, lighting up the room.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Who is it? Music notes surround this balloon.
Say, friend! Why don't you move a little closer to the door?
cbml:panel.note: Soldier attempts to bring the intruder close to the door.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Thaaat's it. Don't be scared. I just want to-
TOK TOK
cbml:panel.note: Soldier attempts to snap the intruder's neck, but fails due to the Hired Hand stepping back.
After a beat, the Hired Hand glances to his watch as Soldier clutches his hands in rage.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Alright, you can come in.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier holds his hands down in defeat.
Soldier unlocks the numerious locks on his door.

div.note: Soldier points a shotgun at the Hired Hand in his barracaded apartment.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Unless you're the tomato soup wholesaler or a new delivery man from the rib place...
...You have just entered a doorway of hurt into an apartment of pain, son.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier's apartment appears to be in disarray, with open cans of army ration soup and open boxes of buckshot strewn about.

div.note: The Hired Hand reveals a television featuring the Administrator. She and Soldier have a tense chat.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Good lord no!
cbml:panel.note: The Hired Hand opens up his trenchcoat, revealing... something glowing.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Tell me, Mister Doe...
CLK
Do you know what a conflict of interest is?
cbml:panel.note: The Hired Hand shows a TV strapped to his chest, featuring The Administrator

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Can I guess?
No.
You don't own me! You just try and stop me, lady.
It is a form of combat!
No.
A breed of dog!
I'm afraid not.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier peers over his table, shotgun aimed at the TV screen.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: It is knowing what words mean! These are guesses!
cbml:panel.note: Soldier continues to aim at the TV as the Hired Hand stands over him.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Mr. Doe. You have befriended a man we are paying you to kill.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator smokes from her cigarette, as viewed through a grainy black and white screen.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: As such, you have two options. One: my associates will drive you to the nearest gravel pit...
OO! That one.
-Where they will kill you for your gross insubordination.
Wait. Let me hear both choices first.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier takes cover behind the table, negotiating with The Administrator.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Option two...
You kill this man. And we supply you with the custom-built weapons you'll need to get the job done.
cbml:panel.note: A close up on the grainy TV, now showing Demoman's face with a sideways glare.

div.note: Soldier attempts to argue with clearly faked videos of Demoman insulting him.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Then I guess you'd better take me to the gravel pit and shoot me, lady.
'Cause if you ever ask me to kill my friend again, I will put my boot so far up your ass it will be on the news.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier throws the table in a fit of rage, getting right up to the Administrator's monitor.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: That's not the option he took from his employers.
He agreed to kill me for weapons? HA! I don't buy it, sister.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier gets up to the TV, pointing at it directly. The Hired Hand continues to hold his coat open.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Listen for yourself.
Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic. *BZZT* I-WILL-KILL-THE-SOLDIER. *BZZT*
cbml:panel.note: A smiling Demoman from the TV.
Soldier seems shocked hearing this.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic. *BZZT* HE-IS-A-BAD-FRIEND. *BZZT*
cbml:panel.note: A smiling Demoman from the TV. Same as on panel 3.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Ahhhh, but dammit- it doesn't matter what he said in that weird robot voice I've never heard him talk in before.
Once you've taken a man out for whiskey and ribs... Then fought him... Then fought the police with him...
Well, you have forged a bond thicker than any soup you can buy.
That's not girl talk, either.
That is just facts.
cbml:panel.note: Soldier monologues, surrounded by cardboard boxes.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: No deal, pumpkin. Find yourself another patsy.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator puts her face in her hands, cigarette smoke billowing out beneath them.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic. *BZZT* HE-IS-NOT-A-REAL-SOLDIER. *BZZT*
Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic. *BZZT* HE-WAS-NOT-EVEN-IN-THE-ARMY. *BZZT*
Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic. *BZZT* HE-IS-A-FRAUD. *BZZT*

cbml:balloon.note: Unlike a normal speech bubble, this is formatted closer to the sound effects made throughout the comic.

cbml:panel.note: Soldier recoils in horror at hearing Demoman's entirely fabricated words.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: How dare he? I earned every one of those medals I made! I did three goddamn tours of duty overseas, and I wasn't even asked! I paid my dues! And my plane ticket over!
cbml:panel.note: A furious soldier rants at the percieved insults of Demoman.

cbml:panel.cbml:balloon: I believe we have a deal, Mr. Doe.
There will be a new weapon waiting for you every day until the job is done.
The first weapon we'll be sending you is a precision instrument.
If you were blasting around randomly, it would be useless to you.
However, I think you'll find it useful for sharp-shooting... specific enemies.
Pauling, kill the feed, please.
cbml:panel.note: The Administrator sits smugly, holding the weapon (the Direct Hit) in her hands.
